SCARLETT VEGA's hand and forearm enter from the right edge of frame, sleeve of her fitted black cotton turtleneck pushed up to the elbow, a thin silver ring on her index finger, fingers still hovering mid-motion just above the tube after releasing it, tendons taut, the gesture caught in the split second before the tube settles against the napkin. Hard directional late-afternoon window daylight rakes in from camera left, undiffused, carving crisp hard-edged shadows off the phone, the tokens, the carton and her fingers across the pale surface, warm cream and oat-beige tones lifted and airy against the bone white, with the single saturated coral accent as the only chromatic punch. Out-of-focus background elements crowd the far top edge of frame — an old enamel sink lip, a kettle, a chipped subway-tile backsplash — dissolved into soft bokeh.
